title: One loss and one gradient for every family
brief: Write the loss A(eta) - y eta and its gradient X^T(mu - y), then fit a Poisson model by walking downhill.
hints: The loss is np.sum(log_partition(family, eta) - y * eta) with eta = X @ w. On the three-row shop data at zero weights it is 3.
The gradient is X.T @ (mu - y), where mu = mean_from_natural(family, eta). On the shop data at zero weights it is [-1, -2].
In gradient_descent_glm, append the loss at zero weights before the loop, then append the loss again after each update, so history has steps + 1 entries.
